pages.text: $(thing)SATTRACK$() lists every $(l:radiocraft:repeaters/satellites)satellite$() on the server and its next passes over the computer: when it rises, how high it gets and which way it comes up, with its three frequencies, tone, mode and decay date.$(br2)It comes on a floppy with every satellite contract, or make one from a blank floppy and a phantom membrane.

pages.title: Controlling yours
pages.text: While your satellite is passing over the computer, its owner and the players on its allowed list can change it:$(li)$(thing)F7$(): on or off$(li)$(thing)F3$(): its Morse ID$(li)$(thing)F4$(): the tone$(li)$(thing)F5 / F6$(): allow or disallow a player$(br)Out of a pass the settings are locked.

pages.title: Its mode
pages.text: An amateur satellite also has a mode, changed the same way while it passes:$(li)$(thing)F8$(): the next mode (repeater, APRS, mailbox, SSTV)$(li)$(thing)F9$(): its APRS frequency (blank for its downlink)$(li)$(thing)F10$(): upload an .IMG to send in SSTV mode$(br)On a commercial satellite F8 switches between repeater and weather $(l:radiocraft:computer/wxsat)imaging$().

pages.title: Telemetry
pages.text: With a radio on the computer's station tuned to a satellite's $(thing)telemetry$() frequency, SATTRACK decodes its beacon while the computer is in use: battery, current, temperature, sunlight or shadow, mode and days to decay. It shows POWER SAVING during an eclipse and a low battery after one, and warns the owner as the orbit nears decay. With Doppler on it shows the downlink's shift.

pages.title: Geostationary and DEAD
pages.text: A $(thing)GEO$() satellite stays put: SATTRACK says it is always up here (and where) or never up from here, with no passes.$(br2)$(thing)DEL$() decommissions one of yours while it passes, the owner only: a question, then a final warning (No is first). It is then listed $(thing)DEAD$() until its orbit decays, and takes no more changes.
